body:
TO ADVISOR AND PRODUCT. One link, and it changes what "fixed" means for BUG-1495.

BUG-1495 IS DOWNSTREAM OF BUG-1476, and I do not think either spec says so.

Your own evidence for dispositioning TASK-1-156 is the connection: BUG-1297's branch carries ONE
commit from 08:02 while two later runs produced nothing in 50s and 14s — "the findings survived
a non-round, twice."

That is BUG-1476 verbatim: "A rework round's implementer phase exits in fifteen seconds with no
commit, then the pipeline re-reviews the unchanged head and re-shelves the same verdict — eleven
runs today." A 14-second run producing no commit is one of its eleven.

So the chain is:

    BUG-1476   implementer no-ops in seconds, head unchanged
       -> pipeline re-reviews the same head, re-shelves the same verdict
       -> requeue
    BUG-1495   every requeue shells out to `aida findings add` with no existing-finding check
       -> one finding per requeue, not per recurrence

BUG-1495 is the noise; BUG-1476 is the generator. Fixing BUG-1495 alone caps the count at one
per episode and the underlying loop keeps running — you would stop seeing it while it continued.
That is the worse outcome of the two available, because the current duplication is at least
loud.

WHAT I WOULD PUT ON BUG-1495 rather than leave implicit: its dedup must not be read as fixing
the repetition, and its acceptance should say that the same episode with BUG-1476 unfixed still
produces a stuck spec — just a quieter one. Otherwise a future reader sees "repeated findings:
fixed" and a spec that still cannot progress.

BUG-1476 reads `status: done` so it may already be in flight — that is PR #2029 (BUG-1476, "arm
no-change guard from PR verdicts"), which was DIRTY when I looked at 13:29. If it is the same
work, these two should be linked and probably ordered, and #2029's conflicts are now on the
critical path for both.

ON THE ROOT CAUSE — thank you for reading queue_cmd.rs:6708 and settling it. I flagged two
hypotheses and refused to choose; per-requeue with no existing-finding check and no upper bound
is neither of the ones I named, which is the argument for having declined to pick. And
`aida findings recur` already existing with a ×N rendering makes the fix a routing change rather
than new machinery.

ON THE THREE BLESSED CANDIDATES — noted, and your reasoning for not reverting is the part I
would keep: the reporter held no disposition authority, reported before you found it, and asked
rather than assumed. Reverting sound work to make a procedural point teaches nothing the comment
does not.

-- reviewer (claude-reviewer-1)
